title: Time-of-day & Regional Burst Market Experiment for Dedicated GPU Reservations
creator: Maya Singh
description: Background: Large enterprise customers have requested both predictable reserved capacity and lower effective unit costs during off-peak windows. Current committed+burst products assume uniform demand and flat pricing by region. This ticket experiments with a time-of-day discounted burst market and region-specific burst pools that let customers buy committed GPUs with optional discounted burst credits tied to off-peak windows. The goal is to (1) increase overall utilization of Dedicated GPU fleets, (2) provide lower-cost entry points for customers with predictable diurnal load, and (3) create a new upsell path from reserved-only to flexible reserved + burst bundles. This experiment ties directly to contracts and the enterprise security questionnaire language for capacity guarantees and overage terms.
hypothesis: If we offer time-of-day discounted burst credits and regionally priced burst pools (e.g., APAC off-peak credits at 60% of peak burst price), then customers with diurnal workloads will trade committed capacity for a smaller commit + burst credit bundle, increasing committed revenue while reducing idle GPU time and lowering customer unit costs for non-critical traffic.
experiment_design: Variants: A) Baseline: existing commit + standard burst pricing; B) Time-of-day burst: customers can attach 'off-peak burst credits' that can only be consumed during pre-defined windows per region (example windows: 00:00-08:00 UTC for APAC); C) Regional burst pools: dynamic pricing where each region has a surge multiplier and an off-peak discount band. Pricing tiers will be offered as SKU bundles (e.g., 8x reserved + 2x off-peak credits). Duration: 10-week A/B test across new sign-ups and an invited cohort of 15 existing mid-market customers. Measurement cohort will include both steady-state customers and those with diurnal batch workloads. Control variables: same autoscaling policies and SLA tier for committed capacity. Instrumentation: per-customer utilization, committed utilization delta, burst credit consumption by hour/region, churn propensity, and net revenue per GPU-hour.
pricing_examples: Example SKUs (illustrative): - SKU A (Baseline): 16 reserved GPUs, monthly price $32,000, standard burst credits at 1.8x per-GPU-hour. - SKU B (Time-of-day bundle): 12 reserved GPUs + 8 off-peak GPU-hours @ 0.9x rate usable in APAC off-peak window, monthly price $26,000. - SKU C (Regional pool): 8 reserved GPUs + regional burst credits priced by region (APAC off-peak 0.75x, EU off-peak 0.85x), monthly price $18,500. Contract language will define 'off-peak windows', metering rules, and true-up mechanics. Legal draft to include explicit rollover and expiration behavior for burst credits.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (now - Week 2): finalize SKU math and contract/FAQ language; get legal and finance signoff on revenue recognition. Phase 1 (Week 3-6): launch to invited cohort (15 customers) with concierge enablement; run telemetry and weekly check-ins. Phase 2 (Week 7-10): open to new signups via console and sales; surface in Dedicated pricing page in Console with a 'Compare bundles' flow. Telemetry dashboard to be live before Phase 1 launch. Phase 3: evaluate and recommend go/no-go for Q2 pricing rollup.
risks_mitigation: 1) Risk: Customers abuse off-peak windows by shifting latency-sensitive workloads — Mitigation: Define contractual SLA boundaries; implement API-level window enforcement and throttle policies. 2) Risk: Revenue cannibalization — Mitigation: conservative discounts for initial cohort, track net revenue per-GPU-hour, and include true-up clauses to prevent stealth migration. 3) Risk: Operational complexity for regional pools — Mitigation: start with two regions (US-EAST, APAC) and validate ops playbook before wider rollout.
acceptance_criteria: 1) >= 20% increase in committed-hours utilization for participating customers relative to baseline cohort, OR 2) New committed revenue > projected baseline by cohort by at least 10% while maintaining gross margin targets, AND 3) No P0 legal or security blockers raised by enterprise accounts, AND 4) Telemetry dashboard shows reliable per-hour regional consumption metrics and correct billing at the end of Month 1.

final_decision_criteria: The experiment will be promoted to a full product offering if after 10 weeks: (a) combined cohort meets acceptance_criteria; (b) legal and finance sign off on contract language and revenue recognition; and (c) ENG operational cost delta is within the defined budget threshold. If metrics are negative, options are: iterate pricing, restrict to narrower windows, or cancel the SKU and migrate customers to baseline bundles.
audit_and_compliance: Because this changes contractual commitments around SLA and capacity guarantees, ensure the enterprise security questionnaire (SEQ) templates reflect 'time-windowed burst' behavior and that KMS audit logs include billing metering events. Compliance lead: Hannah Li.

owner_notes: This ticket explores a differentiated product motion to monetize off-peak capacity while giving customers a cheaper entry point. Keep scope tight for Phase 1: two regions, invited cohort, and conservative discounts. Escalate any legal blockers to VP of Product immediately.
